claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show a three-tier console design consistent with the PS4 Pro model.

claims.claim: twice the GPU power of the standard PS4
claims.evidence: Internal hardware performance and specifications cannot be confirmed through photos.

risks.risk: The consoles may not power on or may have a 'Blue Light of Death' (BLOD) failure.
risks.proof: A video showing both consoles booting to the PlayStation home screen.

risks.risk: The HDMI ports or internal graphics chips may be damaged, preventing video output.
risks.proof: A video showing the consoles connected to a TV and displaying a stable signal.

risks.risk: The optical disc drives may be faulty and unable to read games.
risks.proof: A video of a game disc being inserted, recognized, and launched on each console.

risks.risk: The consoles might be banned from the PlayStation Network (PSN).
risks.proof: A photo of the consoles successfully logged into the PSN Store.

risks.risk: Missing essential accessories like controllers, power cables, and HDMI cables.
risks.proof: A photo showing the consoles alongside all included accessories.

proof_requests: Video of both consoles powering on and displaying the dashboard on a screen.
Photos of the 'System Information' screen showing the software version and 'Storage' screen for both units.
Photos of any included controllers and cables.
Video of a disc being inserted and read by the PS4 Pro.
response.reason: The witness has confirmed the physical presence of a PS4 Slim and a PS4 Pro. They can be priced at the worst-case functional state (non-working, console-only) until further proof is provided.
